_comment: Anthropic API list prices (USD per 1M tokens, input/output) — re-grounded 2026-09-05 from platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview.md (Fable 5.1 $10/$50 · Opus 5 $5/$25 · Sonnet 5 $2/$10 · Haiku 4.5 $1/$5, all four confirmed live). Used by derive_cost.api_equiv and claude_p_cost.api_equiv (the RANKING axis), so a stale figure here silently re-ranks the pool. SONNET was corrected 2026-09-04: the file carried $3/$15 behind a note saying the $2/$10 introductory rate ran 'through 2026-08-31'; the live page lists Sonnet 5 at $2/$10 with NO expiry. CACHE MULTIPLIERS are × the input price. `_cache` is the DEFAULT for every model; `_model_cache` holds per-model-id EXCEPTIONS, which claude_p_cost.api_equiv prefers over the default. The live footnote reads: 'prompt cache reads cost 10% of the base input price (2.5% on Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1)'. That exception cannot live on a FAMILY key: `claude-code/fable` covers both `claude-fable-5` (10%, $1.00 on a $10 input) and `claude-fable-5-1` (2.5%, $0.25), and in the live 30-day window this box ran 76.3% of its fable-tier tokens on claude-fable-5 and 23.7% on claude-fable-5-1 — so a family-level 0.025 would trade a 4× overprice on the smaller share for a 4× UNDERprice on the larger one. Cache reads are 96-98% of real volume, so this is the dominant term, not a rounding error. Claude Mythos 5.1 shares the 2.5% rate but has never run on this fleet and has no row here. ⚠️ A bare tier alias ('fable') is AMBIGUOUS and gets the 0.1 default — pass the full model id to price a cache read exactly. Originally reported as a blind spot by fleet (mail 01M1PTQ5QXJR0AAGW3YYG3HHWE); guarded by tests/test_price_ratios_current.py + tests/test_claude_p_cost.py.
